h1: Tools for listening, imagining and making music
deck: Some musical ideas are worth keeping close. Come back to these maps, sounds and creative tools whenever a lesson—or your own music—gives you a question.
intro: The resources in this library are here to be explored, not memorized all at once. Each one connects real musical knowledge with something you can hear, see and use. Open a quick reference, dive deeper when you're curious, or bring an idea into your next soundscape.
controls: Explore Resources · Back to My Journey · Jump to the Interval Palette.

tile.Title: The Ajourné Interval Palette
tile.Blurb: Hear and compare every interval within an octave. Find its conventional name and semitone distance, explore possible sound qualities, and imagine what it could add to your music.
tile.Subline: 13 landmarks · quick colorful chart · full expandable atlas · original listen/compare exercises

categories: the chromatic keyboard, note names, semitones, whole steps, octaves and sharps/flats. Existing W1-06/07/08 assets can become a later Keyboard Map reference.
melodic gestures, intervals as sequential movement, contour, oblique/contrary/similar motion, and internal-keyboard tracking. Existing W2 and W3 source visuals support later resources.
triads, chord quality, chord roles, changing support, and shared tones, retaining the clear difference between scale function and chord membership.
rhythmic values, pulse/subdivision, entrances, silence, repetitions and form, linked later to actual original audio demos.
short original creative prompts, printable pitch/voice maps, tonal atlas sheets and optional painting.
credited performances, culturally grounded exploration, listening cues and source caveats, curated by lesson rather than a generic international clip gallery.
